content: Euphoria, in the context of emotions, refers to a state characterized by an extremely intense feeling of happiness and well-being. 4-Methyl-aminorex, often referred to as Euphoria or U4EA, is a stimulant drug with effects that are comparable to those of methamphetamine. Euphoria is also the name of a genus of scarab beetles. The term New York Euphoria, previously known as Team Euphoria, refers to a team that participated in the Lingerie Football League. In the realm of music, Euphoria has been used as the title of several albums: Euphoria by Def Leppard, a studio album by the British rock band. Euphoria, a series of trance music compilations released under the Telstar Records label. Euphoric, a 1991 album by the electronic music project Delerium. Several songs are also titled Euphoria: A track by DJ Tiësto from his album Parade of the Athletes. A song by Kyle Ward featured in the video game In the Groove. A track by Collide from their 2003 album Some Kind of Strange. Euphoria (Definite Mix), a song by André Schneider from his 2004 album Lover's Space. A song by Sirenia from their 2004 album An Elixir for Existence. Euphoria (Firefly), a track by Delerium from their 1997 album Karma. The term Euphoria has also been used as the name of various musical groups: EUPHORIA, an American sunshine pop band active during the 1960s. Euphoria, an Australian pop/dance trio that gained popularity in the 1990s. Euphoria, an Indian rock group formed in 1989 and still active.
